What the simulations are saying

  • The favorite is still an underdog to the field. The Colorado Avalanche win the Stanley Cup in 19% of 10,000 simulated postseasons, the best of any club, which means someone else wins it in 81% of them. Sixteen wins across four best of seven rounds is a long way to go, even for the best team.
  • The conference favorites. In the Eastern the Carolina Hurricanes reach the Stanley Cup Final 23% of the time; In the Western the Colorado Avalanche reach the Stanley Cup Final 33% of the time.
  • The wild card race. The club most likely to get in as a wild card is the St. Louis Blues, 40% of the time. A wild card crosses to face a division winner in round one, so finishing third in a division is often the easier road.
  • Too close to call. The Buffalo Sabres (61%), the New Jersey Devils (61%), the Ottawa Senators (60%), the Seattle Kraken (54%), the Florida Panthers (42%), the Nashville Predators (38%) make the playoffs in between 35% and 65% of simulated seasons. Those are the clubs whose next few weeks move the bracket most.

How the 2026-27 NHL playoffs work

Teams earn two points for a win and one for a loss in overtime or a shootout. The top three teams in each of the 4 divisions make the playoffs, and the next two teams in each conference by points take the wild cards, 16 teams in all. The division winner with more points plays the second wild card, the other division winner plays the first, and the second and third place teams in each division meet.

The bracket stays inside the division through the second round, so the first two rounds decide a division champion on each side before the conference final. There is no reseeding. Every series is best of seven, played 2-2-1-1-1 with home ice to the team with more points, and that includes the Stanley Cup Final.

How the bracket odds are produced

The percentage beside each team in the bracket is that team's chance to win that matchup. Every round is a best of seven, and the chance is worked out exactly, game by game, from the model's single game win probability at each arena in the 2-2-1-1-1 order, so home ice counts for what it is worth and no more. Your champion card multiplies every pick you made into the model's odds of that exact bracket, which is why a bracket full of favorites is still a long shot.

The seeds start from the projected standings: every team's average points across 10,000 simulated 2026-27 seasons, from the same game model the NHL Season Simulator uses. Edit seeds lets you set any field you like. The odds table is a different question answered the same way: it plays the regular season and the whole postseason 10,000 times and counts how often each club reaches each round. How the model has scored on a season it never saw is on the season simulator and on the methodology page.

How far to trust the Stanley Cup odds

Treat a Stanley Cup percentage as the least certain number on the page. It multiplies four playoff rounds of close to even games, so a few points of rating error in one club moves its Cup chance far more than its playoff chance, and the 80% ranges above cover both the luck of the schedule and the chance that a team's rating is off: each simulated season moves every club's strength by a random amount sized from past seasons, the same treatment as the NBA and NFL season simulators.

Live, 2026-27: every NHL game since Wednesday, October 7, 2026 has been frozen before puck drop and graded after the final. Through Saturday, October 31, 2026, 174 games, the model's Brier score was 0.2329 against 0.2269 for the no-vig betting market on the same games. The market has been the better forecaster so far, and these season and Cup odds come from the same ratings.

Where the ratings and the market disagree most so far, as the model's win probability minus the market's for that club, game by game: Florida Panthers 13 points lower over 10 games; Boston Bruins 8 points higher over 11 games; New Jersey Devils 8 points lower over 11 games; Toronto Maple Leafs 6 points lower over 12 games; Seattle Kraken 6 points higher over 10 games. A club rated from a 2025-26 season played without injured regulars, or one that changed its roster over the summer, can sit well away from the market until enough 2026-27 games are played, and its season, playoff and Cup percentages carry that error.

Simulations are useful. Verified records matter more.

A simulator can tell you what might happen. It cannot tell you who has actually been right. That is what TrustMyRecord is built for: every pick is locked before the game, graded automatically and counted on a public record, with no deleted losers and no edited history. NHL Playoff Simulator FAQ

What is an NHL playoff simulator?

A tool that plays out the NHL postseason. Here it does two jobs: a bracket picker where you choose the winner of every series through the Stanley Cup Final, and a predictor that simulates the 2026-27 season and playoffs 10,000 times to give every team's odds of reaching each round.

How do I fill out an NHL playoff bracket?

Click a team in any matchup to advance it. Later rounds fill in as you go, and changing an early pick clears only the picks that depended on it. Fill with favorites takes the model's favorite in every open matchup, Simulate the rest draws them from the model's odds, and Edit seeds lets you change the field before you start.

How are the NHL wild cards decided?

After the top three teams in each division, the next two teams in each conference by points are the wild cards. The division winner with more points plays the second wild card and the other division winner plays the first.

Who is favored to win the 2026-27 Stanley Cup?

In the current projection the Colorado Avalanche win it 19% of the time, ahead of the Carolina Hurricanes at 13%. Those numbers move as results come in, and the page is rebuilt twice a day.

Can I share my NHL bracket?

Yes. Share bracket copies a link that carries your seeds and picks, and anyone who opens it sees the same bracket. Your bracket is also kept on your own device, so it is still there when you come back.

Is the NHL playoff simulator free?

Yes. The bracket picker, the projected field and the published odds are always free. Your first simulation on TrustMyRecord is free, with no account needed. After that, a free account gives you one free run a day on every simulator, and each extra run costs 5 TMR. TMR Pro members run every simulator without limits. A run only counts once its result appears, so a run that fails or never finishes costs nothing.
